 No. 4 Herriman (10-2) vs. No. 1 Skyridge (10-1)
 6A semifinals
 Thursday, Nov. 12, 11 a.m., at the University of Utah
 Parry’s Power Guide: Skyridge by 10
 All-time series: Skyridge leads 3-0 (since 2020)
 Last meeting: Skyridge won 43-0 at Skyridge (Aug. 26, 2022, nonregion)
 Herriman overview
 Head coach: Matt Rickards (3rd year, 23-12 record; 94-62 in 14 seasons overall)
 2026 record: 10-2 (second in Region 2 with a 5-1 record)
 2025 postseason: Lost to Mountain Ridge, 22-14, in the 6A quarterfinals
 All-time record: 111-86 (17 years)
 State titles: 1 (2015)
 Region titles: 2 (2013 co, 2019 co)
 What Herriman needs to do to win 
 Davis led for most of last Friday’s quarterfinal, and early in the fourth quarter Herriman’s season was 12 minutes from ending. Then Filisi Filipe took over. His 2-yard touchdown run with 10:10 left gave the Mustangs their first lead, and his 1-yard run with 5:24 remaining finished a 36-22 win. A year after losing 22-14 to Mountain Ridge in the quarterfinals, Herriman is back in the semifinals.
 Filipe is the main reason. He has run for 1,709 yards and 29 touchdowns at 9.1 yards per carry, and with three touchdown catches he has 32 total touchdowns. Max Stevens adds 649 yards. The Mustangs average 38.1 points per game, third in 6A. Bryson Sweeney keeps the offense balanced. He has thrown for 2,013 yards and 21 touchdowns with only five interceptions, and Hayes Priest leads the team with 53 catches.
 The defense allows 16.8 points per game, fourth in 6A. Kemper Castro has 11 sacks, and Ashton Hebert and Aden Jensen have six each. Hebert also returned a fumble for a touchdown in the first round. Logan Gregory and Aden Perea have four interceptions each, and Perea has scored twice on defense.
 The common opponents favor Skyridge. Lehi beat Herriman 22-20 and lost to the Falcons 28-20. Mountain Ridge beat Herriman by 38 and Skyridge by 15. To win, Herriman probably needs to do what it did in the fourth quarter against Davis: lean on Filipe, wear down the defense and keep Jagger Fountaine off the field. 
 Skyridge’s quarterback has thrown 12 interceptions, and Herriman’s secondary can take advantage. In his third season, Matt Rickards has Herriman in the semifinals for the first time under his leadership. The program is chasing its first state title since 2015.
 Skyridge overview
 Head coach: Justin Hemm (4th year, 40-10 record; 66-17 in seven seasons overall)
 2026 record: 10-1 (first in Region 3 with a 4-0 record)
 2025 postseason: Lost to Lone Peak, 13-7, in the 6A semifinals
 All-time record: 110-28 (11 years)
 State titles: 1 (2022)
 Region titles: 5 (2018, 2021 co, 2024, 2025 co, 2026)
 What Skyridge needs to do to win 
 Skyridge has won a lot of close games this season, and last Friday it won another. American Fork was within a touchdown in the fourth quarter. Fountaine threw a 31-yard touchdown pass to Dax Rehrer with 3:31 left, and the Falcons held on 28-21 after Nate Childs found Cash Taiese for a touchdown with 1:55 remaining. Eli Mortensen had an 18-yard touchdown run and a 74-yard catch, and Fountaine accounted for three touchdowns.
 That was the Falcons’ 10th straight win since a season-opening loss at Mountain Ridge. Seven of those wins came by eight points or fewer. The best of them was a 37-27 win over defending champion Corner Canyon, and they also won at Lone Peak and Lehi. They won Region 3 outright at 4-0. Herriman and Skyridge both beat a 5A semifinalist outside 6A: Herriman beat Bountiful 25-14, and Skyridge beat Orem 21-14.
 Fountaine has thrown for 2,791 yards and 25 touchdowns and run for five more. Omarian Sanders has seven touchdown catches, Rehrer has 43 catches, and Beckham Bennett has 802 rushing yards and 13 total touchdowns. Evan Kopp has made five field goals. Skyridge averages 30 points per game and allows 19.4, both sixth in 6A.
 The defense makes big plays. Sa Tanuvasa and Rex Caswell lead the team with 88 tackles each. Sua Ripley has seven sacks. Ethan Schriever has five interceptions and a defensive touchdown, and Jackson Horsley has also scored on defense.
 The challenge is Filipe. Skyridge hasn’t faced a back like him since the opener, and Mountain Ridge was the only team to beat the Falcons by more than a score. Skyridge has to tackle well and get ahead early so Herriman has to throw. Justin Hemm took Skyridge to the 6A title game in his first season. Last year Lone Peak beat the Falcons 13-7 in the semifinals, and this time they’re trying to get past that round. The winner plays the Mountain Ridge–Corner Canyon winner for the 6A championship.

 6A semifinals
 Thursday, Nov. 12, 2:30 p.m., at the University of Utah
 Parry’s Power Guide: Corner Canyon by 12
 All-time series: Corner Canyon leads 3-0 (since 2023)
 Last meeting: Corner Canyon won 59-20 at the University of Utah (Nov. 14, 2025, 6A semifinals)
 Corner Canyon overview
 Head coach: Casey Sutera (1st year, 10-2 record; 45-16 in five seasons overall)
 2026 record: 10-2 (second in Region 3 with a 3-1 record)
 2025 postseason: Beat Lone Peak, 35-20, in the 6A championship
 All-time record: 150-31 (14 years)
 State titles: 6 (2018, 2019, 2020, 2023, 2024, 2025)
 Region titles: 11 (2013 co, 2014, 2017, 2018, 2019, 2020, 2021 co, 2022, 2023, 2024, 2025 co)
 What Corner Canyon needs to do to win 
 Corner Canyon has already beaten this opponent in this round. A year ago at Rice-Eccles Stadium, the Chargers beat Mountain Ridge 59-20 in the semifinals. Helaman Casuga threw for 360 yards and three touchdowns, Jaxon Hunt threw three interceptions, and Jaoquin Rodriguez returned one of them 68 yards for a touchdown. A week later Corner Canyon beat Lone Peak for its third straight state title.
 Most of that team is gone, and so is coach Eric Kjar, who left for Weber State. Casey Sutera took over in his first season as head coach and has the Chargers two wins from a fourth straight championship, which no team in program history has done. Last Friday they beat Syracuse 42-6 in the quarterfinals. Jaxon Pehrson threw a 43-yard touchdown pass to Carter Kjar just over nine minutes into the game, and Corner Canyon led 28-0 at halftime. Jackson Carruth ran for two touchdowns, and Pehrson added a 4-yard touchdown run.
 Corner Canyon’s offense is built on big plays. Pehrson has 35 total touchdowns, 28 passing and seven rushing, and averages 17.8 yards per completion. Beckham Coon averages 26.1 yards per catch and Kelen Gold averages 22.9, and each has seven touchdown catches. Diesel Dart has 11 total touchdowns. Carruth has run for 1,164 yards and 10 touchdowns. Carson Burnett has made six field goals and has 81 points.
 Defense is how Corner Canyon has won before. Wyatt Warner has 15 sacks, the most of any player in the 6A semifinals, and Jack West has six. Will Tenney has three defensive touchdowns, and Josh Harris has two interceptions and two return touchdowns. Tate Patterson leads the team with 97 tackles. As a team, the Chargers have seven defensive touchdowns.
 To win again, Corner Canyon has to pressure Hunt the way it did a year ago. He has thrown seven interceptions all season, so Warner and the pass rush will probably have to force mistakes rather than wait for them. Pehrson also has to protect the ball. He has thrown 12 interceptions, and Mountain Ridge’s defense has scored twice off turnovers. The common opponents favor the Sentinels, especially Skyridge, which beat Corner Canyon 37-27 and lost to Mountain Ridge 41-26. Still, the Chargers have won all three meetings with Mountain Ridge.
 Mountain Ridge overview
 Head coach: Nick Robins (2nd year, 22-3 record)
 2026 record: 12-0 (first in Region 2 with a 6-0 record)
 2025 postseason: Lost to Corner Canyon, 59-20, in the 6A semifinals
 All-time record: 53-36 (8 years)
 State titles: None
 Region titles: 2 (2025, 2026)
 What Mountain Ridge needs to do to win 
 Two years ago Mountain Ridge finished 5-6. A year ago it won its first region title and reached the semifinals, where Corner Canyon beat it by 39 points. Now the Sentinels are 12-0 and haven’t played a close game since mid-October, and they get another chance at the program that ended last season. Nick Robins is 22-3 in two seasons. Before he arrived, Mountain Ridge was 31-33 in its first six years.
 The biggest change from last year is the defense. Mountain Ridge allows 10.3 points per game, the fewest in 6A. It has given up more than 13 points twice all season, and both times it still won by at least 13. Last Friday it beat Lone Peak 42-3, and the Knights didn’t score until the fourth quarter. Cole Uluave and Jayce Helm have four interceptions and a defensive touchdown each. Boston Kojima has six sacks, Kyler Christiansen has four and Scooby Tulau leads the team with 63 tackles.
 Hunt has changed as much as anyone. The quarterback who threw three interceptions in last year’s semifinal has thrown seven in 12 games this season. He has completed 69.2% of his passes for 3,928 yards and 51 touchdowns, and he threw three more against Lone Peak, including an 8-yard score to Tytan DeJong with 19 seconds left in the first half. He has five receivers with at least 500 yards. DeJong has 71 catches and 13 touchdowns. Marshall West has 12 touchdown catches, and Xander Thayer averages 25.7 yards per catch. Tyson Dunn has 803 rushing yards at 9.5 yards per carry. Will O’Neil has made six field goals and has 83 points. The Sentinels lead 6A at 45.6 points per game.
 View Comments Mountain Ridge beat every opponent the two teams shared, and by more than Corner Canyon did. It beat Davis 42-7 and Lehi 42-0, and it beat Lone Peak by 39, while the Chargers beat the Knights by 23. The question is pressure. Warner and Corner Canyon’s front have taken over big games before, and Mountain Ridge has to keep Hunt upright and avoid giving up big special-teams plays. The program is still chasing its first state title. The winner plays the Skyridge–Herriman winner for the 6A championship. Mountain Ridge beat both of those teams this season.
